四级核心词汇 · 10英文原文

The Seal in the Old Bible

旧《圣经》里的印章 · 599 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A museum planned an exhibition on a frontier port the empire had occupied for a century. A crown and a navy map showed the breadth of imperial territory. A label praised the emperor's conquest of a coastal colony. Leena, a junior researcher, found a second account inside an old Bible. It bore a church seal. It ordered the kitchen to feed families whom imperial troops had driven from their homes.

2The chief historian called it a religious record of Christian worship. He thought it had no place beside the royal display. Leena showed him the date. A commander had seized the harbor at the river's mouth the previous day. A priest had made it his mission to keep the church gate open. The cooks could feed any inhabitant in accordance with the order, whether or not the family stayed loyal to its lord.

3A later page described a bitter clash in the castle courtyard. The commander had accused a native soldier of helping a rebel. He planned to execute him. The priest prayed for mercy and offered a witness. The soldier had carried grain during a famine. The commander thought the man had betrayed him until he saw both seals. He let the prisoner go. The soldier's defense had depended on a scrap of paper.

4Leena found the man's name again in a treaty. As an interpreter, he helped negotiate the treaty and overcome a language barrier. A revolution had ended imperial rule. The new republic proclaimed a constitution that promised liberty and civil equality. A revolutionary writer praised the man's resistance, while a royal record called him a faithful servant of the crown. Neither said that he had carried food. Leena asked a scholar to compare the accounts.

5The scholar found a statement by a slave who had later been liberated. He had understood the priest's devotion to Christ through a bowl of food. A noble family had offered silver for the release of one captive. The kitchen fed a whole settlement. Sharing scarce supplies involved sacrifice. A story of combat and conquest alone would conceal the deed that connected the families.

6Leena proposed a cultural display beside the crown. It would show the treaty, the seal, and a list of names from the grain store. The director feared visitors would infer that it condemned every soldier. Leena added a letter from a soldier who helped reinforce the church gate. People could support the invasion and still oppose cruel treatment. The evidence supported a more complex account of the conflict.

7Pupils tested the display before opening. A girl asked why the list was placed behind an imposing stone pillar. Leena moved it to the front. Now an ordinary name had as much space as a royal title. The director saw that a small change to the interior could broaden the story without changing the facts. Her teacher said pupils often studied the glory of a civilization without learning how ordinary people lived. This room could preserve a record of one ancestor who had kept a family alive. Leena added the grain store to the map. In that era it had occupied the busiest part of the street.

8At the solemn opening, a boy asked who had defeated the enemy. His teacher pointed to the map and described the battle. The boy looked at the strip of paper and asked who had opened the gate. Leena read him the priest's order. The crown marked a change in power. The seal recorded a moral choice and its consequences. The boy traced the dates on a calendar and grasped the distinction.

四级核心词汇 · 10中文译文

旧《圣经》里的印章

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1博物馆筹划一场展览，讲一座曾被帝国占领了一个世纪的边境港口。一顶王冠和一张海军地图展示了帝国版图之广。标签赞扬皇帝征服这块沿海殖民地。年轻研究员莉娜却在一本旧《圣经》里找到另一份记录。纸上盖着教堂的印章，命令厨房把饭分给被帝国军队赶出家门的家庭。

2首席历史研究员认为，那只是基督徒礼拜的记录，放在王室展品旁不合适。莉娜把日期指给他看。就在前一天，军队指挥官攻占了河口的港湾。一位神父把保持教堂大门敞开当作自己的职责。按照命令，厨房可以给任何居民分食物，无论那一家是否还效忠他们的领主。

3后面一页记下了城堡院内的一场激烈冲突。指挥官指控一个本地士兵帮助反抗者，准备处决他。神父请求饶他一命，并提出带证人来。那名士兵在饥荒时运送过粮食。指挥官起先以为他背叛了自己，直到看见两枚印章才放了人。士兵能为自己辩解，靠的是一小张纸。

4莉娜后来在一份条约里又看到他的名字。他当了口译员，帮双方克服语言障碍、商定条约。革命已经结束帝国统治，新共和国公布了宪法，承诺自由和公民平等。一位革命派作家赞扬他曾经抵抗，王室记录则说他始终忠于王冠。两边都没提他送过粮食。莉娜请一位学者把记述放在一起比较。

5学者找到一份后来获释的奴隶留下的陈述。从一碗饭里，他看懂了神父对基督的虔诚。一个贵族家庭曾出银子赎回一名俘虏，教堂厨房却为整个聚居地供过饭。物资短缺时，愿意分享就意味着作出牺牲。故事如果只讲打仗和征服，就会把曾经让这些人互相联系起来的那件事遮住。

6莉娜提议在王冠旁加一处文化展陈，摆上条约、印章和粮仓留下的名单。馆长怕来客以为，展览是在谴责每一名士兵。莉娜加了一封士兵的信，那个人曾帮忙加固教堂大门。有人支持入侵，也反对残酷对待居民。证据说明，这场冲突有比单一说法更复杂的一面。

7开幕前，有学生试着参观。一位女孩问，为什么名单放在气派的大石柱后面。莉娜把它移到前方。现在，一个普通人的名字也能和一个王室头衔占一样大的位置。馆长看到，室内做个小调整，事实原样保留，故事也能讲得更广。女孩的老师说，学生常学一个文明有过怎样的辉煌，却不知道普通人怎么生活。这个展厅能保留一位曾让一家人活下去的先人留下的记录。莉娜把粮仓也画到地图上。当年，它占着街上最热闹的地段。

8开幕仪式很庄重。一个男孩问，是谁打败了敌人。老师指着地图给他讲战事。男孩又看看那张纸条，问是谁开了门。莉娜给他念神父的命令。王冠记下权力换了主人，印章则留下一个关于是非的选择及其后果。男孩在日历上描出两个日期，明白了这是两件不同的事。
